title: Minimum Viable Launch (MVL) — stability KPI ladder & ops toggles
content:
Purpose:
This doc defines the Minimum Viable Launch (MVL) acceptance criteria for stability during the first 72 hours, the KPI ladder (baseline → desired → safety thresholds), the per-metric owner map, and a compact set of operations toggles (fast rollback / throttle / degrade) to run if thresholds are breached.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to hosted-api feature rollout v1.2 (token pricing experiment + streaming enabled).
- Target rollout: 5% of traffic for first 48h, then gating decision at 72h.
- Assumes Dedicated fallback pool is available and warm.
- Focused on production-impacting signals: latency, error rate, token cost per request, and quality degradation (eval sampling).

MVL acceptance criteria (all must be satisfied to expand beyond 5%):
1) 95th percentile response latency <= 650ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens).
2) Overall 5xx error rate <= 0.25% (service-level) and per-route errors <= 0.5%.
3) Token cost per successful request within +15% of forecasted burn (forecast model: conservative batch sizing).
4) No >5% regression in quality lift on the baseline prompt set (daily eval sampling).
5) No unresolved P1 incidents open > 1 hour during the window.

KPI ladder (format: metric — baseline | target | safety threshold | owner):
- p95 latency (short) — 580ms | 450ms | 650ms | Rohan Gupta
- p99 latency (short) — 1.1s | 0.9s | 1.6s | Rohan Gupta
- overall 5xx rate — 0.12% | 0.05% | 0.25% | Priya Anand
- per-route error (chat-stream) — 0.2% | 0.08% | 0.5% | Diego Marquez
- token-cost per request — $0.012 | $0.010 | $0.014 | Product Finance (TBD)
- eval quality regression (sampled prompts) — 0% regress | <1% regress | >5% regress | Research/Applied ML (Priya)
- infra warm-pool headroom — 20% | 25% | <10% | SRE oncall

Owner map and quick RACI (single-line):
- Stability monitoring: Priya (R), SRE (A), Eng-serving-runtime (C), Product-ops (I)
- Capacity & scaling decisions: SRE (R), Eng-infra (A), Product-ops (C)
- Consumer communication (status): Product-ops (R), CS (C), Eng-comm (I)

Three-tier response plan (fastest to gradual):
1) Fast toggle (0–10 minutes) — Roll traffic back from 5% to 0.5% via router flag; toggle out streaming for affected route; notify incident channel. Owners: SRE + Product-ops.
2) Mid toggle (10–60 minutes) — Shift route to Dedicated fallback variant (quantized model) with degraded latency but lower cost; reduce max tokens by 30% on in-flight sessions. Owners: Eng-serving-runtime + SRE.
3) Slow toggle (60–240 minutes) — Canary rollback to previous model version; or temporary hold on new feature (disable feature flag at gateway). Owners: Eng-release + Product-ops.

Contingency toggles (implementation notes):
- Router-flag: feature_routing.v2.percent = X — immediate throttling.
- Streaming disable: per-route config stream_enabled=false (graceful degrade).
- Token cap application: request.max_tokens_override=0.7 * requested_max (applies only to non-critical flows).
- Fallback model swap: model_alias -> model_variant_quant8 (pre-warmed).

Runbook (first 2 hours):
- T+0: observe initial 15-minute sampling for p95/p99; check error spikes per route.
- T+15m: validate eval sampling outputs (10 prompts) for quality drift; build quick diffs.
- T+30m: confirm cost burn matches forecast (sliding window); if >10% delta, pre-alert product-finance.
- T+60m: leadership sync (15 min) if any safety threshold breached; recommend one of the 3 toggles.

Dashboard metric definitions (for dashboard owners to implement):
- "p95_short_latency_ms": measured at edge for requests with input_len<=128; window=1m, alert if >650ms for 5 consecutive windows.
- "service_5xx_pct": ratio of 5xx / total requests; window=5m, alert if >0.25% sustained for 3 windows.
- "token_burn_rate_usd": rolling cost per 1000 successful requests; window=30m; alert if > +15% vs forecast.
- "eval_quality_regress_pct": percent of sampled eval prompts with lower score vs baseline; sample size=50/day; alert if >5%.

Pre-launch checklist (dev-ready -> MVL go decision):
- [ ] Dedicated fallback pool warmed and validated against synthetic load (SRE sign-off).
- [ ] Router flag and percentage rollout validated in staging (release engineer).
- [ ] Alerting rules in Grafana/MetricSource created with runbook links (Monitoring owner).
- [ ] Eval prompt set (50 canonical prompts) uploaded and baseline scores committed to confluence (Applied ML).
- [ ] Communication templates pre-written for customer updates (+ internal ops blurb).
- [ ] On-call rotation schedule for first 72h explicit and distributed.

Expansion gating at 72h (decision criteria):
- Positive gate: All MVL criteria met and token burn within forecast +/-10% for the last 24h.
- Conditional gate: One safety threshold hit but mitigated with toggles and trend improving for 12h -> expand to 20% with monitoring.
- Negative gate: Any single metric over safety threshold AND no clear mitigation path -> roll back to 0% and postmortem.

Notes on sampling & quality checks (practical tips):
- Use deterministic seeds for eval sampling so diffs are reproducible.
- Prioritize customer-facing prompts in the sample set for earlier signal.
- Tag eval outputs with model-variant and rollout-percentage for filtering.

Open questions / risks:
- Who is final owner for token-cost alerts? (Finance vs Product ops)
- Are we comfortable with backpressure behavior when streaming is disabled? Need perf QA.
- Do we have a safe automated path to shift to Dedicated pool without losing in-flight state? (Engineering feasibility)

Next steps (this doc -> action):
1) Priya to provision eval set + commit baseline scores (ETA 2024-11-22).
2) SRE to run synthetic warm pool verification and post results (ETA 2024-11-25).
3) Rohan to create the Grafana panels and alert rules; link runbook (ETA 2024-11-27).
4) Leadership go/no-go sync scheduled 2024-11-29 09:00 PT.

Appendix: quick links and shorthand
- Confluence: /pages/viewpage.action?pageId=1234 (MVL playbook canonical)
- Jira: OPS-706 (fallback warm pool work), PROD-1984 (feature rollout tickets)
- Slack: #prodops-launch, #sre-oncall

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally compact and decision-focused. Suggest removing non-actionable rows and converting some owner lines to tickets if we need traceability.
